title: Xenon nuclear response at q ≈ 250 MeV: how form-factor nodes and isotope mixtures shape the inferred couplings
question: At q(248 keV) = 246 MeV, how do the M, Sigma', Sigma'', Delta, Phi'' responses of the Xe isotopes behave, how large are shell-model (WimPyDD/DMFormFactor) vs Helm/2pF differences, how close is the event to the M node, and what nuclear-structure band does this put on the couplings inferred for O1 (elastic, inelastic), O4, O6 and L10?
headline_result: The event lies 19 keV below the shell-model M node at 266.9 keV (isotope spread 251-278 keV; Helm 279, 2pF 309 keV), where the SI response is x5.6 below Helm and dR/dE varies x40 across +-23 keV: O1 couplings from the event carry a nuclear-structure factor ~3 (full ROI) to 5 (window) in coupling^2 (x7 more at 265 keV), whereas Sigma'/Sigma'' responses (L10, O4, O6) have no node near the event and their couplings are robust to +-15%
key_numbers: q=246.4 MeV (243-251 over isotopes); nodes natural Xe shell 102.0/266.9, Helm 94.3/278.9, 2pF 103.3/308.8 keV; shell/Helm F2 0.998(50) 0.335(200) 0.275(225) 0.177(248) 0.114(265); 2pF at matched rms 4.79 fm node 292 keV; 129Xe Sigma' minima 90/375 keV, 131Xe 36/292, Sigma'' none <420 keV; q^4Sigma' kernel peak 233 keV; shares at 248 keV L10 70/30, O4 52/48, O6 40/60 (129/131); window rate alt/shell O1 Helm 4.5, 2pF 10.2 (smeared 3.4/5.6), L10 thin-shell 1.64, O4 0.88, O6 0.48; dR/dE max/min 230-270 keV O1 41, L10 1.8, O6 1.2; full-ROI coupling^2 factor shell/Helm 0.38/0.35/0.30 at delta 250/300/350; delta=300 interval 1.28e-5-2.60e-4 -> 4.5e-6-9.0e-5; L10 Fig.6 bottom linear axis d10 m_v^2 at 1000 GeV 0.154/0.375/0.553 (0.31-3.9 events)
model_or_mechanism: NREFT nuclear response functions (Fitzpatrick/Anand) from WimPyDD per isotope vs Helm and 2pF form factors; per-isotope rate re-weighting exact for velocity-independent operators; window/smeared/full-ROI rate ratios as PLR proxy
